slides.title: The Problem
slides.message: Agent events fire but users can't inject custom logic
slides.visual: mermaid: flowchart showing events passing through without interception
slides.notes: 23 event kinds exist but only SSE/ledger consume them
slides.presenter_script: Before hooks, the event stream was a one-way pipe. Users could observe but never intervene.
slides.common_misconception: You need to modify the runtime engine to add custom behavior
slides.transition: Let's see how hooks solve this

slides.title: HookRegistry Design
slides.message: Composable wrapper: Before-hooks → Inner Sink → After-hooks
slides.visual: mermaid: sequenceDiagram showing event flow through before-hooks, inner sink, after-hooks
slides.notes: HookRegistry implements EventSink protocol — it IS an EventSink
slides.presenter_script: The HookRegistry wraps any EventSink. Before-hooks can block or modify. After-hooks always run for audit.

slides.title: Five Built-in Patterns
slides.message: Protected paths, commands, stop verification, output sanitization, signal injection
slides.visual: table: 5 rows mapping pattern name to what it blocks/modifies
slides.notes: Each is a closure factory — config in, handler out
slides.presenter_script: Five ready-to-use patterns cover the most common frontier harness mechanisms. Register via REST API.
slides.common_misconception: Custom hooks require modifying Python code
slides.transition: How do we keep this safe?

slides.title: Trust and Error Isolation
slides.message: Untrusted = no hooks. Exceptions = caught and logged, event continues.
slides.visual: two-panel: trusted workspace (hooks active) vs untrusted (bypass)
slides.notes: All-or-nothing trust from Claude Code; timeout enforcement per hook
slides.presenter_script: The trust boundary is absolute: untrusted workspaces get zero hooks. And a broken hook never crashes the pipeline.
slides.common_misconception: Some hooks work in untrusted mode
